subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A sonnet is a fourteen-line poetic form.
• Each line follows a specific meter, typically iambic pentameter, and the poem follows a set rhyme scheme.
• "Death Be Not Proud" is a sonnet by John Donne.
• Its rhyme scheme is ABBAABBACDCDEE, characteristic of a Petrarchan sonnet.
• "Shall I Compare Thee" is a sonnet by William Shakespeare.
• Its rhyme scheme is ABABCDCDEFEFGG, characteristic of a Shakespearean sonnet.
prompt: The student wants to use one of the poems to illustrate the sonnet form. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: As a sonnet, "Shall I Compare Thee" contains fourteen lines in iambic pentameter and follows a set rhyme scheme—in this case, ABABCDCDEFEFGG—characteristic of a Shakespearean sonnet.
choices.B: Donne and Shakespeare both employ the sonnet, a poetic form with fourteen lines and a specific meter, in "Death Be Not Proud" and "Shall I Compare Thee."
choices.C: The fourteen-line sonnet form uses the rhyme scheme ABABCDCDEFEFGG, characteristic of a Shakespearean sonnet, which is found in the poem "Death Be Not Proud."
choices.D: Shakespeare has used the sonnet form multiple times, as in "Shall I Compare Thee," which follows this rhyme scheme: ABBAABBACDCDEE.

explanation:
Choice A is correct. It illustrates sonnet form using 'Shall I Compare Thee,' explaining fourteen lines of iambic pentameter with a set rhyme scheme.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. While the sentence appears to use the poem "Death Be Not Proud" to illustrate a feature of the sonnet form, it misrepresents the information in the notes. According to the notes, "Death Be Not Proud" doesn't use this rhyme scheme; it uses a different pattern instead.
